name: Kujong (Couillon)
description: Kujong (known in Belgium as Couillon) is a fast-paced trick-taking card game popular in the Low Countries (Belgium, Netherlands) and parts of Germany and Luxembourg. Played by four players in two fixed teams, it uses a 24-card deck. The game is known for its 'erasing' scoring system, where teams start with a 'tree' of 10-12 branches and aim to be the first to prune their tree to zero by winning rounds.

content.text: Kujong (known in Belgium as Couillon) is a fast-paced trick-taking card game popular in the Low Countries (Belgium, Netherlands) and parts of Germany and Luxembourg. Played by four players in two fixed teams, it uses a 24-card deck. The game is known for its 'erasing' scoring system, where teams start with a 'tree' of 10-12 branches and aim to be the first to prune their tree to zero by winning rounds.
Dates to the 19th century as a simplified variant of the French Jass and Belote families. The name 'Couillon' is Walloon French slang; in Flemish regions, it is often called 'Kwajongen' or 'Troeven'.
4 players in two fixed partnerships (A+C vs B+D).
24 cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 in four suits. Ace is highest (4 pts), King (3), Queen (2), Jack (1).

Each player is dealt 3 cards initially. The next card is turned up for the Trump suit. After the suit is accepted or rejected, each player gets 3 more cards.

items.text: Kwajongen: The Flemish version with identical rules but different terminology.
Troeven: A simplified variant without the 21-point threshold.
